evidence.quote: It was concluded that in Ti-containing RM(Nb)ICs and RM(Nb)ICs/RCCAs, the synergy of Cr, Hf, and Sn promotes the stability of the C14-NbCr2 Laves phase and the formation of Nbss+NbCr2 eutectic in the cast alloys, where the latter is a high-entropy eutectic or a complex concentrated eutectic that forms together with “conventional” phases (see [11]).

the data would suggest that with Ti, Hf, Si, Sn, and Al or Cr additions, the oxidation of RM(Nb)ICs and RM(Nb)ICs/RCCAs (note that the alloy EZ8 is also a RM(Nb)IC/RCCA alloy) can be improved owing to the decrease of VEC alloy.

Compared with EZ1-AC [26], in EZ2-AC the synergy of Ti with Hf and Sn did not affect the solubility of Si in the Nbss and Ti-rich Nbss, but it increased the concentration of Sn in the Nbss by about 1.8 at.%.

Compared with the as-cast Nb-18Si-5Sn (alloy NV9 in [39]), alloying with Hf (alloy EZ1) or with Al (alloy EZ7) or with Hf and Cr (alloy EZ3, see Table 6 for the nominal compositions) shifted the composition of the Nb5Si3 away from the Nb-rich corner
In the alloy EZ3 [26], the synergy of Cr with Sn and Hf destabilized the Nbss + Nb5Si3 eutectic and instead resulted in the formation of a Nbss + C14-NbCr2 Laves phase eutectic (Table 7).

However, the addition of Hf in the alloys EZ1 [26] and EZ2, despite the fact that it did not completely destabilize the A15-Nb3X, essentially rendered its formation sensitive to cooling rate, probably due to the fact that Hf affected the Si+Sn and Si/Sn values that control its formation.

the Ti addition in EZ5 had a significant effect on the partitioning of Hf, and the concentrations of Ti and Hf increased by, respectively, about 8.1 at.% and 6.3 at.% in the Hf-rich Nb5Si3, leading to Nb/(Ti + Hf) about 0.7, which indicated hexagonal γNb5Si3 [24].
